verdict.rationale: React's markup is JSX, a JavaScript syntax extension that lives inside the script itself rather than a separate template [react-docs-2]. Adding @types/react and @types/react-dom gives 'full React Web support' for TypeScript [react-docs-13], which implies markup is type-checked along with the rest of the code. However, no evidence explicitly states that JSX elements, props or expressions are checked at compile time. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that TypeScript type-checks JSX markup and props, details of the type-checking workflow (tsc/editor errors in markup), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
